name: India National Air Quality Index (CPCB)

sources.title: CPCB, About National Air Quality Index (categories and breakpoints for 8 pollutants)
CPCB, AQI-Calculator.xls (official calculator; formulas decoded from BIFF records)

categories.label: Satisfactory
categories.health: Minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people.

categories.label: Moderately polluted
categories.health: Breathing discomfort to people with lung or heart disease, children and older adults.

categories.label: Poor
categories.health: Breathing discomfort to people on prolonged exposure.

categories.label: Very poor
categories.health: Respiratory illness to people on prolonged exposure.

categories.label: Severe
categories.health: Respiratory effects even on healthy people.

rules: Sub-index is piecewise linear and continuous: each band runs from the previous band's upper breakpoint (e.g. PM2.5 30 to 60 maps to index 50 to 100). This matches the official calculator's formulas.

Above the last breakpoint, the slope of the last band continues (e.g. PM2.5 > 250: 400 + (C - 250) x 100/130). The calculator does not cap at 500, so neither do we; the UI shows values above 500 as '500+'.
AQI = max sub-index, published only when at least 3 pollutants are available and one of them is PM10 or PM2.5 (calculator note).
24-h averages for PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, NH3, Pb; maximum 8-h rolling mean within the trailing 24 h for CO and O3 ('max 8-hr' in the calculator).
AQI is reported as an integer, rounded half-up.
notes: Two official documents disagree. The 'About AQI' text says PM2.5 31 gives sub-index 51, which uses the EPA-style formula from the band's own lower bound. The calculator gives 51.67. We follow the calculator because it is the tool CPCB distributes for computation. The difference is at most 1 index point, at the start of a band.

Calculator typo fixed: its O3 > 748 branch computes 400 + (C - 400) x 100/539, which jumps from 400 to 465 at 748. We use (C - 748). The calculator also divides by 539 for 208-748, a span of 540. We use 540, a difference of 0.2 index points at most.
Minimum data completeness (16 of 24 hours, 6 of 8 hours) is our implementation choice. It follows CPCB's 2014 AQI report as quoted in secondary sources; we could not reach the primary report.
Pb is part of the standard but no source in our regions reports it in real time.
